items.topic: Garbage-collection rule for abandoned manualReview=true sandboxes
items.context:
The auditability contract says `manualReview=true` sandboxes MUST persist beyond run end until the operator approves or denies. The contract intentionally leaves the GC rule to this item. Without an upper bound, abandoned pending-review sandboxes leak overlay storage indefinitely. Workspace-sandbox already has a `gc/` package and `PolicyConfig.TeardownHooks`; we'd add a single new policy lever.

Note: This is the most consequential 'open detail' the contract leaves to this item.

options.label: TTL from run end (default 7 days)
options.rationale: Simple, predictable, easy to audit. After 7 days post-run-end with no operator action, the sandbox auto-denies all pending files and is torn down. Matches operator intuition ('AI Changes are still here a week later? safe to drop'). Configurable via `WORKSPACE_SANDBOX_MANUAL_REVIEW_TTL`.

options.label: Idle timeout (no operator views/touches the run for N days)
options.rationale: More forgiving for runs operators do briefly look at but don't decide on. Requires tracking last-viewed timestamps on the provenance record (small schema add). More complex but lower false-positive GC rate.

options.label: No automatic GC; operator-only teardown
options.rationale: Safest data-preservation stance. Forces explicit operator action. Operationally risky — pending-review sandboxes accumulate forever; storage growth is unbounded; needs an alert at minimum to be tolerable.

options.label: Hybrid: TTL + per-org override + alert at 75% of TTL
options.rationale: Belt-and-suspenders. TTL gives the upper bound, alert gives operators a chance to act, override lets specific teams hold longer. More config surface; more code; more docs.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own GC rule (specify TTL, trigger, override behavior, and what 'GC' does — auto-deny + tear down, just stop, or something else).

items.topic: Migration approach for the existing field surface (Acceptance.AutoApprove/AutoReject/DisableAutoApproveIfEmpty + RunConfig.RequiresApproval)
items.context:
The locked contract names new per-run levers (`mode`, `manualReview`, `autoApply`, `applyOnFailure`, `lock`, `networkMode`). Today, agent-manager has overlapping, partially-functional fields:
- `SandboxAcceptanceConfig.AutoApprove` / `AutoReject` / `DisableAutoApproveIfEmpty` (drives `tryAutoApproval` in run_executor.go)
- `RunConfig.RequiresApproval` (gates whether the auto-approval path runs at all)

The new levers express the same semantics more cleanly. We need to decide whether to replace, deprecate, or layer.

options.label: Replace wholesale (greenfield) — remove old fields, add new ones, update all call sites
options.rationale: Matches CLAUDE.md's greenfield default. Cleaner code surface. No deprecated aliases to maintain. Forces every caller to articulate the contract explicitly. Risk: breaks any persisted Run / RunConfig records mid-flight; upgrade story is 'roll the change atomically'.

options.label: Add new fields alongside old; old fields take precedence if set; deprecate via godoc
options.rationale: Lower-risk for in-flight runs and external callers. Two field surfaces to keep in sync; precedence rules invite drift. Likely to leave dead code for months until a follow-on cleanup item runs.

options.label: Add new fields; auto-derive new from old if old is set; prefer new if both
options.rationale: Preserves existing run records' semantics but normalizes new ones. Most complex of the three; mapping logic must round-trip cleanly; tests get harder.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own migration approach (e.g., 'replace but feature-flag for one release', 'rename Acceptance.AutoApprove → AutoApply with a typed Migrate() helper', etc.).

items.context:
This item writes provenance with `runOutcome` (run group) and per-file `state` (∈ applied / pending-review / denied). Those fields are owned by `execute/gct-pending-ai-provenance-hardening` (upstream initiative `git-control-tower-ai-provenance`). The spec says the schema can land 'first or in parallel'. We need to pick.

Observable contract — the AI Changes review queue, per-file state badges, and runOutcome rendering — is gated on the schema landing AND this item's writes hitting the new fields. Without coordination, one side ships data the other can't read or vice versa.

options.label: Block this item until schema lands (serial)
options.rationale: Simplest. No feature flags. No half-state. This item's tests assert against the real schema. Slows down the calendar but the engineering is cleanest. Recommended unless the schema work has explicit slack.

options.label: Parallel with a schema-version contract; both items merge in any order
options.rationale: Faster. Requires a small typed contract (e.g., a shared proto / Go interface) that both items target. Each item ships its side; integration tests gate on both. Harder to coordinate; more PR-review overhead.

options.label: This item ships first against a stub provenance writer; schema item replaces the stub
options.rationale: Decouples agent-manager's PR cadence from GCT's. Stub provenance is observable (logs, dev metrics) but operators see no value until schema lands. Risk: stub diverges from real schema and the swap is non-trivial.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify your own sequencing (e.g., 'land schema in this PR series and absorb gct-pending-ai-provenance-hardening into this item', 'split this item into a writer-side and a queue-side ticket', etc.).

items.topic: Apply trigger placement in the run executor lifecycle
items.context:
Today, `handleSuccessfulCompletion` calls `tryAutoApproval` (which dispatches to `autoApprove` / `autoReject` / `autoApproveIfEmpty`). Failure / cancellation / timeout paths SKIP apply entirely. The new contract says apply behavior is identical for all four `runOutcome` values when `manualReview=false`. We need to pick the right place to insert the new apply call.

Key constraint: the trigger must run exactly once per run, regardless of which terminal handler fires (success / failure / cancelled / timeout).

options.label: New `applyAtRunEnd` step called from a single shared point (e.g., end of `Execute()` after all terminal handlers, gated on RunMode==Sandboxed && manualReview==false)
options.rationale: Single call site = single source of truth for the apply contract. Easiest to test (one method, one path). Matches the contract's 'identical regardless of outcome' framing structurally. Replaces the existing `tryAutoApproval` indirection cleanly.

options.label: Call `applyAtRunEnd` from each terminal handler (handleSuccessfulCompletion, handleFailure, handleCancellation)
options.rationale: Keeps existing handler structure. Three call sites — easy to forget one when adding a new outcome. Tests must cover all three handlers. Tighter coupling between outcome classification and apply flow.

options.label: Wrap `tryAutoApproval` to extend it instead of replacing it
options.rationale: Smallest diff. Preserves existing branching. Works against the greenfield directive. The old indirection becomes dead weight; the new fields layer on top of legacy behavior.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify your own placement (e.g., a dedicated phase like RunPhaseApplying after HandleResult, a deferred call wired to ctx.Done, etc.).

items.topic: Mapping domain.RunOutcome (7 values) to the contract's runOutcome (4 values) for provenance
items.context:
agent-manager's `domain.RunOutcome` has 7 values: `success`, `exit_error`, `exception`, `cancelled`, `timeout`, `sandbox_fail`, `runner_fail`. The contract's `runOutcome` field on `ProvenanceRunGroup` has 4 values: `success`, `failure`, `cancelled`, `timeout`. We need a mapping rule.

The lossy collapse only matters for what GCT renders to operators in AI Changes; it does NOT affect apply behavior (contract says 'identical regardless of outcome').

options.label: {success}→success; {cancelled}→cancelled; {timeout}→timeout; {exit_error, exception, sandbox_fail, runner_fail}→failure
options.rationale: Treats every non-clean terminal state that isn't an explicit cancel/timeout as 'failure' for operator visibility. Matches the contract's bucket count exactly. Simplest rule; least surprising for operators reading AI Changes.

options.label: Same as A but {sandbox_fail, runner_fail}→cancelled (since the agent never got to run)
options.rationale: Distinguishes 'the run failed during agent work' from 'the run never got off the ground'. Operators may find this clearer for triage. Asymmetric with the cancelled label's plain meaning ('user cancelled').

options.label: Add a 5th value `infrastructure_failure` to the contract for {sandbox_fail, runner_fail}
options.rationale: Most expressive; matches reality. Breaks the contract — would need a contract amendment back through `gct-pending-ai-provenance-hardening` and the AI Changes UI. Highest churn cost.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify your own mapping. State which agent-manager values map to which contract values and why.

items.text: Existing infrastructure largely already aligns with the contract: (1) `setupWorkspace` already creates the sandbox eagerly at run start for sandboxed runs (line ~619-711 of run_executor.go); the only missing piece is the eager *provenance* write. (2) `SandboxEnvVars` already injects `VROOLI_SANDBOX_ID/MERGED/SCOPE` correctly. (3) `noLockFromSandboxConfig` correctly defers to the workspace-sandbox server default. The bulk of this item's churn is in the apply-trigger path, the field surface, and the new provenance metadata — the eager-creation half of the contract is mostly already implemented.

RunMode (`sandboxed` / `in_place`) is preserved as-is in this item. Flipping the default to `sandboxed` across spawn surfaces (UI, swarm-manager queue, cron, CLI) is `execute/agent-manager-default-sandboxing-rollout`'s responsibility. This item only ensures that when a run IS sandboxed, the contract is honored end-to-end. In-place runs continue to skip the approval workflow entirely (run_executor.go:1423-1426).

plan_updates: Round 1 created the initial plan.md scaffold. Filled all 13 mandatory sections from the auditability contract (Findings 1-6) and the spec. Identified the five core decisions that the spec leaves open or ambiguous: GC rule for manualReview=true sandboxes (the explicitly-open detail), migration approach for the legacy field surface, sequencing with the GCT schema dependency, apply-trigger placement in the run lifecycle, and the RunOutcome mapping. Acceptance globs already set on spec; no acceptance_deny needed. Required Reading section embeds 4 discovered skills (seam-discovery-and-enforcement, test, boundary-of-responsibility-enforcement, implementation-plan-authoring). Greenfield declaration, cleanup & verification phase, and cross-initiative implications all populated.
